# FNB-ETAF repository guidance

FNB-ETAF is an enterprise Java 21 and Maven test automation framework. It supports web UI, API, database, mobile native, mobile browser, XML, CSV, ZIP, PDF, protocol-level API performance, concurrent real-browser UI performance, and governed reporting/evidence.

## Preserve working framework contracts

- Make minimal, targeted, backward-compatible changes. Reuse existing steps, methods, configuration, and YAML resources before creating new abstractions.
- Do not modify Hooks, BrowserFactory, standard runners, browser lifecycle, report lifecycle, video lifecycle, @LastScenario behavior, or TestNG/Cucumber execution technology unless the task explicitly requires that coordinated change.
- Do not change normal UI, API, DB, mobile, PDF, file, performance, or reporting behavior while solving an unrelated defect.
- Add a focused regression test before changing lifecycle, concurrency, shared error handling, or other cross-cutting behavior.
- Keep feature files readable and business-focused. Keep selectors, request bodies, queries, data, and environment configuration in the approved resource directories.

## Safety and confidentiality

- Never put passwords, tokens, cookies, authorization values, customer data, account details, real internal endpoints, screenshots, videos, or report output into source-controlled instructions, example features, YAML, prompts, or generated code.
- Use placeholders such as https://<approved-target> and ${SECRET_FROM_CI}. Never bypass TLS validation, authentication, WAF/rate limits, or application security as an automatic fix.
- Treat generated Copilot advice as guidance only. Preserve code review, architecture review, and normal test validation.

## Required validation

- Compile before presenting a Java change: mvn clean test-compile -DskipTests.
- Run focused tests that cover the changed behavior. Do not weaken tests or thresholds simply to make a build pass.
- Run git diff --check before delivering changes.
- Do not claim an internal application run passed unless the actual approved run completed successfully and its result was verified.

## Optional local Playwright MCP discovery

- Use the local Playwright MCP workflow only when a human explicitly enables it in IntelliJ, approves the exact non-sensitive target origin, and confirms the read-only locator-discovery purpose.
- Playwright MCP is not part of FNB-ETAF runtime. It must not be started by a framework runner, Hook, BrowserFactory, Maven lifecycle, CI pipeline, or generated test.
- Use the approved target alias already maintained in src/test/resources/config/config.yml. Never copy a resolved URL into instructions, generated drafts, feature files, reports, or source code.
- Inspect only a non-sensitive test view. Do not log in, submit forms, type values, accept dialogs, upload/download, capture screenshots/PDFs/videos, collect page source, inspect network traffic, access storage/cookies, or run arbitrary browser JavaScript.
- Never use persistent browser profiles, CDP endpoints, extensions, storage-state/secrets files, TLS-error bypass, unrestricted file access, proxy changes, service-worker persistence, or cloud coding agents for this workflow.
- Generate only review-only locator and clean feature drafts beneath .fnb-etaf/discovery-drafts. Never edit active locators, feature files, configuration, Hooks, BrowserFactory, runners, reports, or tests automatically.
- A human must confirm locator stability and copy approved entries into active test resources, then run the focused test manually.

## Architecture overview

- Production framework code: src/main/java/com/ptaf.
- Cucumber steps and runners: src/test/java/com/ptaf.
- Standard test resources: src/test/resources.
- Standard UI locators: src/test/resources/elements.
- Standard configuration: src/test/resources/config/config.yml.
- Normal browser lifecycle: com.ptaf.hooks.Hooks and com.ptaf.utils.BrowserFactory.
- Protocol/API performance: com.ptaf.performance with resources under src/test/resources/performance.
- UI performance: com.ptaf.ui_performance with resources under src/test/resources/ui_performance. It is deliberately isolated from normal Hooks, normal browser lifecycle, and standard Cucumber reporting.
